subject: Aurora Health — Access controls & SSO/SCIM/IP allowlist handoff
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <p.desai@aurorahealth.com>, IT Security <it-security@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-15 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Aurora Health access plan and constraints

Hi Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the intro. Quick context: we’re doing a phased rollout of Redwood for internal clinical tools across three regions. Security wants the following resolved before a pilot:

- SSO via SAML with strict audience/recipient validation
- SCIM provisioning limited to a single service account and scoped group writes
- IP allowlist for the pilot set (three static egress ranges) and a documented emergency bypass procedure
- Service accounts for batch inference with short-lived keys and audit hooks

I attached the network ranges and a first-pass list of service accounts we expect to create. Can we get a short implementation plan with timelines and the owner for each item?

Goals: pilot in prod-sim environment by 2028-05-10, go-live for pilot org by 2028-05-31.

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurora Health

Attachments: aurora_network_allowlist.csv; initial_map_service_accounts.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-16 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Aurora Health access plan and constraints

Thanks Alex — and great to meet you over email. Looping in Neha (Implementation lead) and Ben (Security & Ops) to map owners. Draft plan below — high level, happy to expand into a canary schedule once you confirm the three ranges and confirm a SCIM admin account.

Planned owners / milestones:
- SSO (SAML): Owner: Neha Kapoor. Deliverables: metadata exchange, IdP certificate rotation window, test IdP connections. Target: 2028-04-22 for IdP metadata import and basic SAML assertion test.
- SCIM provisioning: Owner: Ben Carter. Deliverables: SCIM service principal creation, attributes map (email, role, manager), provisioning scope limited to pilot group. Target: 2028-04-24 for test sync.
- IP allowlist & emergency bypass: Owner: Auror a IT security (you), Redwood Ops point: Ben Carter. Deliverables: allowlist ingestion, temporary VPN/SSH jump procedure doc, monitoring alert rule. Target: 2028-04-20 for allowlist ingestion into staging; emergency bypass runbook by 2028-04-21.
- Service accounts / key policy: Owner: Ben Carter. Deliverables: naming conventions, rotation cadence (30d), audit event hooks to your SIEM. Target: 2028-04-25 to validate short-lived token flow.

Questions for you:
1) Can you confirm the SCIM admin account (email) that Redwood should use and whether you prefer push or pull provisioning?
2) For SAML, do you require encryption of assertions?
3) Do pilots require IP-based geofencing or just the three egress ranges?

Next steps: Neha will schedule a 30-min technical alignment session (SAML + SCIM) for early next week and Ben will share a checklist for the allowlist ingestion.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | Helping teams run LLMs reliably

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-17 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Aurora Health access plan and constraints

Alex — quick confirmation from my side and a couple of specifics for your security team.

1) SCIM: we support both push and pull. Given your org model we recommend push (Redwood initiates writes) scoped to a single service principal with group-filtering. If you want to keep full control, we can do pull (Aurora calls our SCIM endpoint) but that requires a fixed IP allowlist entry and mutual TLS.

2) SAML: we support encrypted assertions. Best practice for healthcare customers is to enable assertion encryption + signed responses. We will need your IdP metadata (saml metadata file). If you prefer, I can send a metadata template for your IdP team.

3) IP allowlist: the csv looks good — we can ingest into our staging environment. For emergency bypass we provide a short-lived (1 hour) token-based uplift that is logged; it requires approval from two Aurora admins. We will send the approval webhook details for your SIEM.

4) Service accounts: recommend short-lived workload tokens integrated with your KMS if available. We can emit audit events to a forwarder (Syslog/HTTPS) — Jordan will own the audit-forwarder integration on Redwood side.

I attached a sample SAML metadata file to speed your IdP team.

Ben Carter
Security & Integrations Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sso_saml_metadata.xml

From: Priya Desai <p.desai@aurorahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.com>, IT Security <it-security@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-20 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Aurora Health access plan and constraints

Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Aurora Security:

- SCIM admin: please use scim-service@aurorahealth.com for provisioning. We prefer push provisioning from Redwood.
- SAML: we will provide encrypted assertions and signed responses. ETA: IdP metadata by EOD 2028-04-18 (sent as separate email and attached to this thread).
- IP allowlist: confirmed ranges (see attached csv) for staging. For prod we will provide a separate set; we expect Redwood to support staged allowlist deployment (staging -> prod).
- Emergency bypass: two Aurora approvers required is fine. Please share the webhook spec and expected alert payloads.
- Service accounts: we will expose a KMS-backed signing endpoint; please provide the naming pattern and token lifetime you need.

Action items we’ll take:
- Tim (IT Security) will add Redwood staging egress CIDRs to our firewall and test connectivity
- I’ll send the IdP metadata and the SCIM admin mailbox now
- We will land a signed PDF of the pilot scope for procurement by 2028-04-22

Marissa — can you confirm whether Redwood needs any org-level policies (e.g., role mappings) in advance or whether we can provide those during the SCIM attribute mapping session?

Thanks,
Priya Desai
IT Program Manager
Aurora Health

Attachments: aurora_network_allowlist.csv (staging)
